consensus_findings.description: Critical: an orphaned setup reservation permanently blocks every sync point with no expiry, GC, or operator escape. `setupReservation` carries only `created_at`/`updated_at` — no TTL, no `expires_at` — while `specs/worktree/spec.md` ("Provisioning reservation blocks sync points") and the CLI `safety_invariants` make an unpublished reservation an indeterminate blocker. Reconciliation is reserved exclusively to the original actor: setup-and-acquire states "Retry reconciles only the exact same setup_id, generation, and requested triple" and "a different setup or controller MUST NOT consume, overwrite, or clean up those side effects". No command in `commands:` operates on reservations (there is no reservation list/abandon/reconcile), `recovery adopt`/`force-adopt` key on entries, and the GC invariant mentions only retained entries. Unlike leases, whose bounded 30-minute TTL is the whole point of D4, a reservation left behind by a controller that never returns is unbounded — reintroducing precisely the permanent sync-point deadlock this change exists to remove, and doing so on the crash path rather than the happy path.

Critical: the feature-HEAD completion barrier is unowned — it has no declaration in the artifact the scheduler actually reads. `contracts/prerequisites.yaml` puts `execution_gate.completion_visibility: feature-head` and `dependent_base_rule: exact-verified-feature-head` in a contract file, but `wp-baseline-preflight` in `work-packages.yaml` declares only `worktree: {name: phase-lifecycle-baseline-preflight, mode: shared}` — no barrier field, no completion-visibility field. Task 0.5 is written as "packages **declaring** a feature-HEAD barrier are not marked complete until…", yet nothing declares one. `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/dag_scheduler.py:142` copies `package.get("worktree", {})` through verbatim and `mark_completed()` (line 343) has no notion of a commit, HEAD, or branch lock; `mode: shared` appears nowhere else in any `work-packages.yaml` in the repository and is interpreted by no code. As written, the barrier requirement in `specs/skill-workflow/spec.md` ("Prerequisite Evidence SHALL Be Visible Before Dependent Dispatch") is untestable because the scheduler cannot tell which packages it applies to.

The setup reservation pipeline atomically bridges Git worktree creation and process evidence without intermediate unleased state. Reservations store a timestamp-free lease_intent, conservatively block sync points as indeterminate provisioning, and derive lease timestamps from the final publication transaction.

Lease ownership is strictly bound to the exact (owner, lease_id, controller_instance_id) triple across acquire, resume, renew, release, teardown, and recovery. Expired takeover requires proof of stale same-host process evidence and clean durable state, issuing a fresh lease and controller identity while force-adoption appends to an immutable recovery audit.

Autopilot run recovery state is stored outside disposable worktrees under monotonic generation CAS and requires proving the exact live registry triple and entry generation before mutation. Recreating a removed checkout validates the exact durable ref tip SHA against durable_head and hashes the raw loop state blob prior to worktree instantiation.

The prerequisite preflight completes as an authoritative feature-HEAD barrier in the shared feature worktree, verifying merge ancestry and surface assertions under the branch lock before satisfying DAG dependencies or constructing dependent package worktrees.

PR delivery stage classification uses a 4-way truth table over changed files and base state, failing safe to ambiguous on diff truncation or marker conflict. Operator overrides are restricted to ambiguous state, bound to RFC-8785 canonical classification digests (pr-delivery-v1+jcs-sha256), and append invalidation events to operator_override_history whenever SHA or ruleset bindings change.

Critical: two requirements in the same delta spec give contradictory worktree rules for the preflight package. "Implementation Orchestrator Worktree Setup" (MODIFIED) states "The implementation orchestrator SHALL create a dedicated worktree and fenced lease for **every root or parallel work package** before mutation", while "Prerequisite Evidence SHALL Be Visible Before Dependent Dispatch" (ADDED) states "The authoritative prerequisite preflight SHALL execute as a **root package in the managed shared feature worktree**". A conforming implementation cannot satisfy both for `wp-baseline-preflight`. `work-packages.yaml` compounds the ambiguity by giving the package both `mode: shared` and a package-specific `worktree.name: phase-lifecycle-baseline-preflight`, which is the naming of an isolated per-package checkout, not the shared feature checkout. An implementer following the MODIFIED requirement will produce an isolated preflight whose verified commit is not feature HEAD — silently defeating D15's stated rationale ("its verified commit is feature HEAD rather than an isolated result awaiting final integration").

Critical: no command can dispose an entry that has no activity lease, and the existing `teardown --force` path is silently dropped. The contract makes `--owner`, `--lease-id`, `--controller-instance-id`, and `--entry-generation` all required for `teardown`, but three documented states have `activity_lease: null`: normalized v1 entries, compatibility `setup` entries (which the contract explicitly says store a null target and stay unleased), and every entry that `release-session`/`release-owner`/unsafe finalization has quarantined-and-cleared. For those, no lease id exists to supply. The recovery route is also closed for legacy state: `recovery adopt` requires stale same-host process evidence, and a v1 entry has no evidence file at all ("missing … evidence is indeterminate" → exit 7), forcing `recovery force-adopt`, which for a null durability target "require[s] durability-remote and durability-ref together, validate[s] and fetch[es] that exact bound target" — impossible for a legacy branch that was never pushed. Separately, today's `skills/worktree/scripts/worktree.py` teardown carries `--force`, documented in its own help text as "Used by POST /agents/{id}/kick to clear stale entries"; the contract omits it and the worktree spec says teardown "SHALL NOT use force to bypass the condition", while `safety_invariants` still assumes "an existing explicit operator force path" exists. Migration compatibility is asserted only for setup, branch override, isolation detection, and package layout — teardown is not covered.

Critical: the inventory fails its own completeness rule, and one real consumer sits outside every package's write scope. The MODIFIED invariant says the inventory "SHALL cover every canonical consumer of setup, heartbeat, pin, active-agent, and registry state and automated tests MUST fail for an unclassified consumer". Scanning canonical sources finds unclassified consumers: `agent-coordinator/src/coordination_api.py` (its `/worktrees/active` docstring encodes the exact semantics being removed — "Omits stale entries (heartbeat > 1h); pinned entries always included"), `agent-coordinator/src/event_stream.py:197` (publishes the worktree projection to SSE clients under the key `active_agents`, a UI-facing activity label), `agent-coordinator/src/sync_points.py` (touched by tasks 5.1/5.2 but absent from the inventory, which lists only `worktrees_view.py` under `coordinator-projections`), `skills/context-engineering/SKILL.md`, and `skills/worktree/SKILL.md`. In the other direction, `project-context-refresh-sync-point` is classified as a consumer although `skills/project-context-refresh/SKILL.md` has no registry or active-agent usage. Worse, neither `coordination_api.py` nor `event_stream.py` appears in any package's `write_allow` (`wp-coordinator-projections` allows only sync_points/worktrees_view/openspec_proposals_api/kanban_viz/Dockerfile/tests), so the required removal of stale pinned-as-activity prose and labels cannot be performed in scope. Additionally, `session-hooks` is classified `registry_reader`, but D10 and the "Session Finalization" requirement have it invoke `release-session`, which quarantines entries and clears leases — a mutation no reader mode permits.

Critical: the `quarantined` envelope transition is the one autopilot recovery write that a stale controller can still make. D9 fences only two classes: "Every `present` or `teardown_pending` envelope mutation also proves the exact live registry owner/lease/controller triple plus entry generation before CAS", and after registry deletion "only the expected `teardown_pending -> removed` CAS is allowed, bound to unchanged envelope generation, lease id, entry generation, and finalization intent". `checkout_state: quarantined` is written after quarantine-plus-clear, when no live registry lease remains to prove — so the registry-triple precondition is by construction unavailable, and D9 states no substitute binding for it. A displaced controller holding `lease-old` that reloads the latest envelope generation therefore satisfies the only stated guard (monotonic CAS) and can drive an actively resumed run — one that legitimately rotated to `lease-new` via `lease resume` — into `quarantined`, where D9's own rule ("Partial presence, `teardown_pending`, quarantine, missing/non-durable refs, or identity mismatch remains escalated") makes it unrecoverable without operator action. This is exactly the stale-controller write the design elsewhere takes care to prevent.

Critical: Autopilot recovery specifies that unsafe teardown first clears the registry lease into quarantine and only then CASes the external envelope to checkout_state=quarantined. Present/teardown_pending envelope writes are gated on the live registry ownership triple, which is gone after that clear, and unlike the explicit identity-bound teardown_pending→removed CAS (envelope generation + lease_id + entry_generation + finalization_intent) the plan never defines authorization for teardown_pending→quarantined. A generation-only CAS would let a stale controller that reloads the latest envelope poison recovery state; requiring a still-live triple would make the legitimate unsafe-teardown path impossible.

Schema v2 registry readers maintain seamless backward compatibility with v1 entries, mapping legacy pinned=true to GC retention while reserving active status for unexpired leases or fresh legacy heartbeats. The pin and unpin aliases remain non-blocking GC controls without granting write leases.

The mutating skill inventory comprehensively classifies all 24 repository-mutating entrypoints and consumers across standalone, continuous, child, hybrid sync-point, sync-point, and registry-reader modes, backed by automated scan tests that prevent unclassified lifecycle drift.

Nit: resume is not specified to refuse a completed run. The schema's second `allOf` branch permits `checkout_state: removed` together with `finalization_intent: done`, and D9's recreation rule keys only on removed state plus exact-tip equality: "resume verifies the currently configured remote URL digest, fetches the stored ref, and requires its tip to equal `durable_head` exactly … recreates the worktree and registry entry … and only then dispatches", continuing "from the phase derived from canonical state". The corresponding spec scenario scopes itself to "ESCALATE or exception finalization recorded `checkout_state=removed`" but nothing forbids the `done` case. Re-invoking a run that already reached DONE and opened its PR would recreate the disposed checkout, take a new lease, and re-dispatch phases against a branch the human merge gate already owns.

Nit: task 2.8's declared file scope exceeds its package's write_allow, so the task as written cannot be executed inside `wp-lifecycle-consumers`. Task 2.8 targets "inventory-owned launcher skills under `skills/`, excluding `skills/autopilot/**` and `skills/merge-pull-requests/**`", which literally includes the `standalone_owner` entries `plan-feature`, `implement-feature`, `iterate-on-plan`, `iterate-on-implementation`, and `validate-feature`. None of those paths appear in `wp-lifecycle-consumers.scope.write_allow`; they belong to `wp-phase-lifecycle`, which migrates them in task 2.2. The scope checker will either reject the writes or the agent will interpret the exclusion list as exhaustive and re-migrate skills another package already owns.

Nit: whether the continuous autopilot lease carries a `session_id` is never decided, and the two artifacts that touch it assume opposite answers. `lease acquire`/`setup-and-acquire` make `--session-id` optional; D9 lists what autopilot passes into every phase (owner, lease id, controller id) and never mentions a session id. The skill-workflow scenario "Session end releases only matching owners" assumes autopilot's session id is "different or null" and must be left untouched, while D10 explicitly contemplates the opposite — "If it quarantines a continuous checkout, later resume preserves the envelope/registry mismatch and remains ESCALATE until explicit reconciliation." Since autopilot runs inside an orchestrating session, the choice decides whether an ordinary interrupted run resumes cleanly or requires `recovery force-adopt` with actor, rationale, and termination confirmation every time.

Optional: the preflight package edits the scheduler it depends on, from the checkout that scheduler is running in. `wp-baseline-preflight` declares `mode: shared` (design D15: "runs in the managed shared feature worktree") and its write set includes `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/dag_scheduler.py` and `integration_orchestrator.py`. Task ordering compounds this: 0.3 runs the live resolver and commits `baseline-gates.json` to gate dependents, but the barrier that is supposed to enforce that gating is only implemented in 0.5, two tasks later. For this change's own coordinated run, the scheduler in effect while `wp-pr-delivery` and `wp-phase-lifecycle` are unblocked is either the pre-change scheduler (no barrier) or a mid-edit one. The `depends_on` edges still serialize dispatch, so the risk is bounded, but the stronger guarantee the plan advertises — dependents created from the exact verified feature HEAD — is not actually in force during the change that introduces it.

Nit: contracts/mutating-skill-inventory.yaml classifies session-hooks as mutation_mode registry_reader and inherits defaults finalizer=teardown-or-quarantine / setup_owner=shared-phase-lifecycle. Design D10 and skill-workflow require session hooks to invoke only release-session as a non-destructive crash backstop and never phase finalization or teardown. Treating hooks as pure readers (or as teardown finalizers via defaults) will mis-shape inventory completeness tests and can authorize the wrong hook contract.

Nit: contracts/cli/worktree-lifecycle.yaml setup-and-acquire both requires exact setup-id/generation/triple retry to complete or report success idempotently after reservation, checkout, evidence, publication, or response-loss crashes, and also says 'Refuse when an entry already exists; callers must use assessed acquire, resume, or explicit recovery instead.' A literal reading of the refuse rule breaks post-publication response-loss recovery that the worktree and skill-workflow specs require.

Nit: coordinator-kanban-viz states that sync-point blockers are a live schema-v2 activity lease or a fresh legacy heartbeat, while design D15, worktree 'Provisioning reservation blocks sync points', active-agent tasks 1.5–1.6, and coordinator task 5.1 require unfinished setup reservations to be indeterminate non-activity blockers. Reusing the canonical active-agent check is helpful but the normative blocker enumeration still omits reservations and there is no coordinator scenario for them.

The revision-5 lifecycle contract now separates timestamp-free setup intent, active ownership, retention, indeterminate provisioning, quarantine, and append-only recovery audit while preserving exact generation and controller fencing at every mutation boundary.

Autopilot recovery now validates derived identity before I/O, authorizes present and pending writes against the live registry fence, uses generation CAS and durability barriers, and permits removed-checkout recreation only at the exact fetched checkpoint tip.
The authoritative prerequisite preflight is a managed shared-feature root package whose owned scheduler completion barrier records and verifies exact feature HEAD before dependent worktree creation.

Delivery routing preserves immutable discovery evidence, current classification, active operator disposition, and append-only record, honor, and invalidation history while rejecting overrides for clear classifications.

The eight-package DAG assigns every mutating launcher, sync point, registry projection, generated mirror, contract fixture, and quality gate to an explicit non-overlapping implementation surface with test-first ordering.

Nit: two task traceability references do not resolve against the delta specs. Task 2.3 cites `skill-workflow` — "Package integration proves parent-ref durability"; no scenario of that name exists in any spec file (the nearest is "Worktrees are finalized after integration" under "Implementation Orchestrator Worktree Setup"). Task 1.1 cites "Activity lease commands respect environment isolation", which is a Requirement heading, not a scenario; the scenario is "Lease mutations short-circuit under harness isolation". Traceability checks and reviewers matching tasks to acceptance scenarios will silently drop coverage for the package-durability behaviour, which is the exact contract task 2.4 implements.

Nit: the classification schema enforces one row of the truth table and leaves the two equally mandatory rows to producers. The top-level `allOf` encodes `marker_status ∈ {conflicting, duplicate, invalid} → delivery_stage: ambiguous`, but the merge-pull-requests truth table's first row ("incomplete, truncated, or failed" required evidence → `ambiguous`) has no corresponding constraint on `evidence.diff_status`, and `evidence.base_state.inspection_status`/`head_state.inspection_status == failed` — which D11 says "are represented explicitly and always yield `ambiguous`" — is likewise unconstrained. The asymmetry is a trap: a producer bug that stamps `implementation` on a truncated diff passes schema validation, and the contracts README's "Producers additionally enforce the exhaustive truth table" is the only thing standing between that bug and an unsafe archival route.

FYI: nothing states the retention policy for `.git-worktrees/.autopilot-runs/<run-id>/recovery.json`. The envelope lives beside the registry inside `.git-worktrees/`, which `worktree.py gc` walks, yet the GC safety invariants speak only of registry entries and retained worktrees, and D9 never says when an envelope in `checkout_state: removed` with `finalization_intent: done` is deleted. Over time the directory accumulates one entry per run, and a GC implementation that treats unknown `.git-worktrees/` children as sweepable could delete a `teardown_pending` envelope that is the only record able to reconcile a crashed teardown.

The package-teardown durability proof is achievable against the repository's actual integration strategy. D8 requires that successful package integration "first pushes the parent feature ref, then proves the exact package HEAD is reachable from its stored parent-feature durability target", and `skills/worktree/scripts/merge_worktrees.py:217` integrates with `git merge --no-ff`, which preserves the package tip as an ancestor of the feature branch. The rule therefore holds without changing integration topology, and the contract's decision to store the parent feature remote ref as the package entry's durability target ("Package and automatic workflow callers MUST use setup-and-acquire and store the parent feature remote ref as the durability target, not a disposable child branch") correctly avoids requiring child branches to be pushed under their own names.

Timestamp-free setup intent traces cleanly and consistently from schema through CLI, design, and spec. `leaseIntent` deliberately omits `acquired_at`, `last_heartbeat`, and `expires_at` while requiring the full ownership triple, and its `lifecycle_mode` enum is correctly narrowed to `standalone|continuous` (excluding `manual`, which only recovery leases use). `setupReservation` carries its own `created_at`/`updated_at` so reservation age is observable without ever implying lease liveness. The CLI's setup-and-acquire step says publication derives `acquired_at` and `last_heartbeat` from one timestamp and `expires_at` from that timestamp plus the intent TTL, D2 says the same, and the worktree scenario "Fresh automatic setup publishes through a durable reservation" asserts it as an acceptance criterion. Four artifacts agree with no drift, which closes the class of bug where a lease appears to have been alive during a long checkout creation.

Operator-override binding and append-only invalidation are complete and internally consistent across schema, design, and spec. The `deliveryRouting` `allOf` forces `decision_source: classifier`, a null override, and blocked review/validation/cleanup routes whenever `effective_stage` is `ambiguous`; the state-level branch permits an override only while `latest_delivery_classification.delivery_stage` is `ambiguous` and otherwise pins `decision_source: classifier` with a null override, matching D15's "clear proposal, implementation, or mixed classifications require classifier routing and reject an override". `selected_stage == effective_stage` is enforced per stage rather than assumed. `operatorOverride` binds all five values D15 names (base_sha, head_sha, ruleset_version, `pr-delivery-v1+jcs-sha256`, digest), and `operatorOverrideEvent` requires the observed counterpart of each plus a `reason_code` enum that covers every mismatch class the spec enumerates — so the invalidation audit cannot be written without the evidence that justified it, and the history survives the override being cleared.

Optional: Task 0.5 and skill-workflow talk about packages declaring a feature-HEAD completion barrier, but work-packages.yaml has only prose on wp-baseline-preflight and the sole machine-readable signal lives in contracts/prerequisites.yaml (execution_gate.completion_visibility). openspec/schemas/work-packages.schema.json has no barrier field, so the scheduler declaration surface is easy to hardcode incorrectly.

Optional: Normalized LEGACY leases store controller_instance_id=null and may renew through the heartbeat compatibility handler without a controller, but lease release and teardown always require a non-empty controller_instance_id. Operators can clear those leases only via release-owner, expiry, or recovery adopt—not exact-triple release—which is workable but easy to miss beside the LEGACY renew exception.

Timestamp-free setup is implementable end-to-end: lease_intent omits acquired_at/last_heartbeat/expires_at, the registry schema rejects timestamped intents via additionalProperties:false, setup reservations advance reserved→checkout-created→evidence-created without granting activity, and the final locked publication derives all lease timestamps from one publication time before replacing the reservation with the active entry.

Live-lease ownership is consistently fenced across acquire, same-controller retry, resume with new fence after stale same-host evidence, renew/assert/release conflicts, teardown-before-release, atomic quarantine-plus-clear, session/owner bulk quarantine, and recovery adopt/force-adopt with null-target establishment and append-only force-adopt audit that survives entry teardown.

Removed-checkout autopilot resume is exact-tip safe: durable_head and loop_state_sha256 are required for teardown_pending/removed, recreation demands current URL digest match plus freshly fetched ref tip equal to durable_head (not mere reachability), and the loop-state blob is hashed and schema-validated at that OID before worktree creation or lease acquisition.

The shared feature-HEAD preflight completion barrier is owned and sequenced: wp-baseline-preflight is a shared-mode root package, depends_on edges gate wp-pr-delivery and wp-phase-lifecycle, tasks 0.1–0.5 cover fail-closed PR evidence plus scheduler barrier behavior, and prerequisites.yaml names the blocked packages and dependent_base_rule.

Delivery routing, append-only override invalidation, inventory coverage, and package DAG are coherent: the classifier truth table and merge-plan schema force stage-consistent routing, overrides are ambiguous-only with SHA/ruleset/JCS digest bindings, invalidation appends history before clearing, inventory enumerates standalone/continuous/child/sync-point/reader consumers with a dedicated migration package, and parallel package write scopes do not overlap once baseline and registry complete.
